newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Light crude ample, heavy market over.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Light crude ample, heavy market over.

text.p: Asian crude trading was quiet with the July market for the heavy grades almost over, traders said on Monday.

Only July cargoes of light crudes, mainly Tapis, Harriet/Copper Basin and New Zealand condensate were still on offer, but will probably be rolled over into August, as most refinery demand for July was covered.
A July Cossack cargo, previously heard to have been sold, was confirmed going into the seller's own system, with the seller still offering a July spot cargo of Kutubu.
Potential interest for the cargo was heard from China.
Traders were surprised by China's appetite, since it had already bought three cargoes of Cossack/Kutubu and more than 500,000 barrels per day of Minas for July.
There were rumours a shosha sold an August cargo of Bach Ho crude at a hefty premium of OSP +60, but it could not be confirmed. July Bach Ho has traded 40/45 cents over the OSP.
In the Middle East market, refiners welcomed Kuwait's decision to cut its crude term formula to Asia, the first change in several years, they said.
There was speculation other Gulf suppliers could follow suit.
Oman, Saudi Arabia and Qatar are due to announce their official retroactive June crude prices later this week.
Spot trading was lacklustre apart from the Oman and Qatar deals done late Friday.

But traders expected the Oman and Abu Dhabi prices to weaken further in August, since two majors who are usually the main buyers, have already bought a large volume of West African and Qatari Al-Shaheen crudes.
